freshness_notes.bgs: BGS GeoIndex current/beta checked 25 July 2026; professional users are still directed to current GeoIndex while beta evolves; SOBI is open and continuously receives new records.
freshness_notes.bng: Statutory biodiversity metric guidance updated 14 July 2026; <=0.2ha development exemption starts 6 August 2026, and NSIP BNG starts 2 November 2026.
freshness_notes.lnrs: London LNRS is published and includes a Local Habitat Map; mapped opportunity locations create no new designation, protection or landowner obligation.
freshness_notes.climate: UKCP guidance updated through February 2026; Local 2.2km projections are available regridded to 5km and official guidance recommends considering surrounding grid cells and uncertainty.
freshness_notes.rail: ORR station usage April 2024-March 2025 published 4 December 2025; passenger rail usage January-March 2026 published 18 June 2026.
freshness_notes.active: TfL Cycling Infrastructure Database is London-wide and current open-data guidance remains available; Healthy Streets remains planning-assessment context rather than a parcel access guarantee.
freshness_notes.heat: Ofgem heat-network regulation is live in 2026; heat-network zoning implementation regulations are still being prepared and DESNZ is building a future zoning pipeline.
freshness_notes.enfield: Enfield BNG, ecological assessment and climate/biodiversity planning guidance checked July 2026; national future exemption dates are preserved over older local wording.
freshness_notes.havering: Havering BNG and Climate Change Action Plan 2024-27 are current council sources; local BNG wording is cross-checked against the later national 6 August 2026 exemption change.
freshness_notes.lambeth: Lambeth biodiversity page now includes Pollinator Action Plan 2026; Climate Action Plan, BNG monitoring-fee and ecology/planning guidance checked July 2026.

query_preparation.promotion_rule: Official map/API/register/download capability may be VERIFIED or PREPARED_QUERY, but exact candidate result remains pending until candidate-specific spatial/habitat/station/asset/address/record evidence and provenance are captured.

batches.c: GeoIndex can query geology, boreholes and hazard-related layers by area. Exact candidate selection is required; map context is not a site investigation.
BGS Geology 50K is local-to-regional geological mapping. Exact polygon binding is screening evidence, not foundation design evidence.
Superficial deposits can affect ground conditions but mapped units remain generalised and require project-specific ground investigation.
SOBI indexes boreholes, shafts and wells. A nearby historic borehole is contextual evidence only until exact record, depth and log relevance are checked.
GeoIndex includes site-investigation reports and borehole records. Record availability does not prove comparable ground conditions at the candidate.
BGS warns open map data have quality and completeness limitations. Ground-risk conclusions remain fail-closed without site-specific investigation.
The statutory metric measures habitat biodiversity value. Exact habitat parcels, condition and proposal inputs are required before calculating candidate units.
Where BNG applies, the statutory objective is at least 10% uplift. This is not a pre-computed parcel score and must follow the statutory metric.
The new <=0.2 hectare planning-application exemption starts 6 August 2026. On 25 July it is future law and must not be applied early.
Mandatory BNG for NSIPs starts 2 November 2026. It must remain separate from current Town and Country Planning Act development rules.
BNG can combine onsite, registered offsite gains and statutory credits under rules. Candidate cost or deliverability cannot be inferred without scheme habitat facts.
Metric tool version, publication date and evidence inputs must be retained. No biodiversity units are invented from mapped context alone.

batches.t: London LNRS Local Habitat Map exact-location prep
batches.c: The Local Habitat Map identifies potential measure locations and biodiversity importance layers. Exact candidate intersection is required.
Potential measure locations create no new designation, protection or landowner obligation; they are strategic nature-recovery opportunities.
LNRS Areas of Particular Importance combine protected nature information, but the page notes source information has a reference date; current detailed source data should prevail.
LNRS can inform strategic significance in BNG, but exact metric application still requires statutory metric inputs and current policy status.
The next London Plan evidence base includes May-July 2026 nature/green-infrastructure evidence. Evidence studies are not themselves adopted site policy.
UKCP Local gives spatially detailed climate projections, not parcel forecasts. Exact grid selection, scenario and time horizon must be explicit.
Future precipitation can inform resilience screening, but local projections should be interpreted with uncertainty and surrounding grid boxes.
Projected maximum temperature is scenario evidence for future overheating risk, not a measured candidate temperature.
Local projections sample a limited uncertainty range; results should be contextualised against other UKCP products and not presented as deterministic forecasts.
Planning FRAs must apply relevant climate-change allowances by vulnerability, epoch and flood source; exact candidate flood context and proposal lifetime are required.
ORR station reference data identify mainline stations. Exact candidate-to-station relation requires a verified station record and access route, not name proximity.
Entries/exits and interchanges are annual station-demand estimates based mainly on ticket sales. They do not measure candidate walkability or service capacity.
Station usage is estimated and revised under a published methodology. Values must retain year and methodology rather than being treated as exact footfall.

batches.t: ORR current passenger-rail usage context gate
batches.c: January-March 2026 national passenger usage is current network context, not a station-specific development-demand forecast.
Station attributes support infrastructure screening, but exact accessibility, step-free route and service pattern need station-specific current records.

batches.t: TfL Cycling Infrastructure Database nearest-asset prep
batches.c: CID maps cycle lanes, tracks, parking, crossings, filters and other assets. Exact candidate route relation is required.
A nearby cycling asset does not prove a continuous, safe route to destinations. Network continuity must be verified separately.
Healthy Streets is a planning/design approach for walking, cycling and public transport. It is not an exact parcel score by itself.
Vision Zero and road-improvement programmes provide strategic context; candidate risk requires exact road/collision/design evidence.
Current consultations and planned Healthy Streets projects are future interventions and must not be counted as delivered candidate accessibility.
Ofgem heat-network consumer regulation is live in 2026. Regulatory status does not establish that a heat network serves the candidate.
A candidate can only use heat-network evidence after exact network/operator and physical connection opportunity are verified.
National zoning modelling identifies opportunity areas. Opportunity modelling is not a statutory designated zone unless and until zoning regulations/designation apply.
DESNZ is developing a future zoning pipeline while implementation regulations are being prepared. Pipeline presence is prospective, not current connection obligation.
Heat-network technical standards and assurance requirements affect network design/operation, but do not prove site feasibility or capacity.
Enfield requires BNG information for applicable applications. Exact proposal date, size and national exemption status must be resolved first.
Protected species, habitats, SINCs and green corridors can trigger ecological assessment. Exact site/neighbouring-feature relation is required.
Local biodiversity priorities support design context but are not a substitute for statutory site survey or BNG metric evidence.
Blue-green network objectives support resilience and nature recovery but do not create a parcel-specific development entitlement or score.
Older local wording must be read alongside the national 6 August 2026 exemption change; future national rules are not applied before their effective date.
Havering requires statutory BNG information for applicable schemes. Exact application date, site size and exemption status are mandatory inputs.
Havering guidance reflects long-term BNG securing requirements. Exact habitat delivery mechanism and planning permission are required.
The 2024-27 action plan addresses climate response and emissions. Borough targets do not become parcel-specific costs or benefits.
Current council environmental programmes and progress are strategic/local context; project status must not be generalized to unrelated candidates.
Local BNG text predates the 6 August 2026 <=0.2ha exemption; national effective dates control and are preserved.
Lambeth identifies local biodiversity assets and SINCs. Exact candidate proximity/intersection and current designation source are required.
The 2026 Pollinator Action Plan is current strategic biodiversity context, not an automatic development constraint or BNG unit value.
Where S106 secures post-approval BNG, Lambeth states monitoring fees are case-specific. No candidate fee is calculated without a real scheme and agreement.
The Climate Action Plan sets borough goals for net-zero compatibility and resilience. These are strategic goals, not parcel-level measured outcomes.
Lambeth planning guidance includes a wildlife assessment check. Exact proposal/site inputs are required before deciding whether professional ecological advice is needed.
